result.summary: This urban street features narrow sidewalks on both sides, with residential row houses on the left and industrial or vacant land on the right. The environment lacks dedicated pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb extensions, or buffers from the parallel-parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the path of the narrow sidewalk on the left, creating obstacles for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking on both sides limits visibility between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian space and encourage safer crossing behavior.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a standard concrete sidewalk adjacent to parallel on-street parking, but lacks any buffer from the roadway. The streetscape is dominated by a large brick building behind a chain-link fence, creating a blank frontage that limits natural surveillance and makes the area feel isolated.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A line of parked cars along the curb blocks the sight lines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground along the curb line

hazards.name: Blank Frontage and Lack of Surveillance
hazards.description: The long chain-link fence and windowless lower section of the brick building create a 'dead' street edge, reducing safety through lack of eyes on the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Background, spanning the length of the block

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the nearest intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the parking lane to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: If pedestrian volumes warrant, install a marked midblock crossing with signage and potentially a pedestrian-activated beacon.

result.summary: The street features narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to parallel parking and travel lanes with no physical buffer. There are no marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures visible, creating a car-centric environment with limited protection for people walking.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalk
hazards.description: The walkway on the right is narrow and lacks a buffer from the roadway, placing pedestrians close to moving traffic.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to increase visibility and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility crosswalks to designate safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from moving traffic and improve the walking environment.

result.summary: A narrow residential street with row houses built directly to the sidewalk edge. The pedestrian environment is constrained by utility poles located within the walkway and a lack of physical buffer from the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are positioned in the middle of the narrow sidewalk, creating obstacles for pedestrians and reducing accessible width.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk on the left side of the street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk to provide a clear through-zone for pedestrians, separate from utility infrastructure.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees in a new furniture zone to provide a buffer between pedestrians and parked or moving vehicles.
